From 53ad4a948a4586359b841d607c08fb16c5503230 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Yuhao Huang <nekowong743@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jan 2026 12:03:48 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] gpio: virtuser: fix UAF in configfs release path

The gpio-virtuser configfs release path uses guard(mutex) to protect
the device structure. However, the device is freed before the guard
cleanup runs, causing mutex_unlock() to operate on freed memory.

Specifically, gpio_virtuser_device_config_group_release() destroys
the mutex and frees the device while still inside the guard(mutex)
scope. When the function returns, the guard cleanup invokes
mutex_unlock(&dev->lock), resulting in a slab use-after-free.

Limit the mutex lifetime by using a scoped_guard() only around the
activation check, so that the lock is released before mutex_destroy()
and kfree() are called.

Fixes: 91581c4b3f29 ("gpio: virtuser: new virtual testing driver for the GPIO API")
Signed-off-by: Yuhao Huang <nekowong743@gmail.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20260126040348.11167-1-yuhaohuang@YuhaodeMacBook-Pro.local
Signed-off-by: Bartosz Golaszewski <bartosz.golaszewski@oss.qualcomm.com>

diff --git a/drivers/gpio/gpio-virtuser.c b/drivers/gpio/gpio-virtuser.c
index 37f2ce20f1ae..098e67d70ffa 100644
--- a/drivers/gpio/gpio-virtuser.c
+++ b/drivers/gpio/gpio-virtuser.c
@@ -1682,10 +1682,10 @@ static void gpio_virtuser_device_config_group_release(struct config_item *item)
 {
 	struct gpio_virtuser_device *dev = to_gpio_virtuser_device(item);
 
-	guard(mutex)(&dev->lock);
-
-	if (gpio_virtuser_device_is_live(dev))
-		gpio_virtuser_device_deactivate(dev);
+	scoped_guard(mutex, &dev->lock) {
+		if (gpio_virtuser_device_is_live(dev))
+			gpio_virtuser_device_deactivate(dev);
+	}
 
 	mutex_destroy(&dev->lock);
 	ida_free(&gpio_virtuser_ida, dev->id);
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a use-after-free (UAF) vulnerability in the GPIO virtuser configfs release path. The single-file modification is in `drivers/gpio/gpio-virtuser.c`.

**Modifications in the file:**

- In function `gpio_virtuser_device_config_group_release()`, the original code used a class-based `guard(mutex)(&dev->lock)` that protected the entire function body. This caused the mutex to be still locked when `mutex_destroy()` and `kfree()` were called, leading to `mutex_unlock()` on freed memory upon scope exit.
- The fix replaces the `guard(mutex)` with a `scoped_guard(mutex, &dev->lock)` that limits the mutex’s lifetime to only the critical section where the device’s live state is checked and possibly deactivated. After this block exits, the mutex is released before `mutex_destroy()` and `ida_free()` are invoked, eliminating the use-after-free.

**Relationship between modifications:**

The core relationship is the **reduction of the locking scope**. By narrowing the mutex protection to only the operations that require it (the activation check and deactivation), the subsequent resource cleanup (mutex destruction and memory deallocation) is performed safely outside the lock’s lifetime. This prevents the premature freeing of the device structure while the mutex is still held, resolving the UAF.

Here is the commit message:
gpio: virtuser: fix UAF in configfs release path

The gpio-virtuser configfs release path uses guard(mutex) to protect
the device structure. However, the device is freed before the guard
cleanup runs, causing mutex_unlock() to operate on freed memory.

Specifically, gpio_virtuser_device_config_group_release() destroys
the mutex and frees the device while still inside the guard(mutex)
scope. When the function returns, the guard cleanup invokes
mutex_unlock(&dev->lock), resulting in a slab use-after-free.

Limit the mutex lifetime by using a scoped_guard() only around the
activation check, so that the lock is released before mutex_destroy()
and kfree() are called.

Fixes: 91581c4b3f29 ("gpio: virtuser: new virtual testing driver for the GPIO API")
Signed-off-by: Yuhao Huang <nekowong743@gmail.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20260126040348.11167-1-yuhaohuang@YuhaodeMacBook-Pro.local
Signed-off-by: Bartosz Golaszewski <bartosz.golaszewski@oss.qualcomm.com>

Here is the root cause:
The guard(mutex) macro's automatic cleanup calls mutex_unlock() on a mutex that has been destroyed and its containing memory freed, because the critical section included the mutex destruction and device deallocation.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void gpio_virtuser_device_config_group_release(struct config_item *item)
 {
 	struct gpio_virtuser_device *dev = to_gpio_virtuser_device(item);
 
-	guard(mutex)(&dev->lock);
-
-	if (gpio_virtuser_device_is_live(dev))
-		gpio_virtuser_device_deactivate(dev);
+	scoped_guard(mutex, &dev->lock) {
+		if (gpio_virtuser_device_is_live(dev))
+			gpio_virtuser_device_deactivate(dev);
+	}
 
 	mutex_destroy(&dev->lock);
 	ida_free(&gpio_virtuser_ida, dev->id);
 	kfree(dev);
 }
